answer_key: `gc` inventories and deletes unreachable objects without fencing against lock-free `Transaction::commit`, so objects and operations published just before their op-head file is written can be pruned mid-commit.

answer_key: `Repo::merge_plan` marks a settler merge's rebase of a post-fork commit as `undone` whenever another side still shows the original commit (`r.commands.is_empty() && shown.contains(&k.0)`), discarding the settler's rebase.

head: 955dcc29b894adf1280e8610a263975c9f90c944
answer_key: `Materialised::fill_in` treats directories left out by `vl clone --only` the same as server-refused directories in `self.hidden` and walks their unfetched subtrees, failing one-directory clones when the working copy updates.

head: 23e64a53e9495a807368195051640b42960a8d2c
answer_key: `Transaction::reconcile_sealing` is bypassed by `keep_sealing` during `split` and trusts any parent blob in `known_secret_ids` regardless of path, producing snapshots with sealed entries at non-secret paths that the server's push check refuses.

answer_key: `settled::record` queries `graph_missing_below` after `persist_index` may have dropped the graph index when a withheld parent arrived concurrently during commit, recording an incomplete missing-parent list so an ancestor head stays unmerged.

head: 31859727f23196f731676c93e43588f7132efe23
answer_key: `ObjectStore::read_packed` and `has_main` test whether the pack directory settled via `reload_packs` against the shared `self.packs` set, so another thread's concurrent reload makes the listing appear unchanged and returns `Missing` without searching the newly installed pack.

head: 9b3cb235520dca8e5b8d92f4cdf5f378ea74945b
answer_key: `Introduced::add_rebases` classifies any value reachable through a merge operation's `rewritten` map from one parent as the merge's own rebase even when another parent already held that value from a command's `describe` or amend, causing a concurrent rewrite or move to overwrite it silently.

head: 9d4f29a94fb2c502e398465cf2a83333d21111ee
answer_key: `hub::Client::new` reads `VEIL_TOKEN` from the process environment ahead of per-authority stored credentials, sending that bearer session token to any remote Veil server regardless of which server issued it.

head: 4bcfd5c97956345e3bd76c3d94b8c050b9d1ce5c
answer_key: `Client::send` caps `503 warming` retries at a fixed `RETRIES` count (8 attempts, ~64 s) without checking whether the server's graph fill is making progress, causing default thin `vl clone` of large repositories to abort mid-fill.

head: b0ace803116850d4289308266be9a9d7e1255b15
answer_key: `hub::pull_moving` prefetches a fresh thin clone's trees via `client.subtree` directly from the server even when the local Veil daemon is active (`daemon.is_some()`), bypassing the daemon's shared tree cache.

head: 6c3467d227a177ff374fff90210977d2dd4127d4
answer_key: `Daemon::renew` polls `objects:batch` every 1 second (`POLL`) for up to 15 minutes (`KEEP_MS`) per used grant epoch even while idle and ignores `429`/`503` `retry_after_ms`, burning the user's per-device server rate budget.

head: eb055df27249c35acd7924558798e387ba9f0f79
answer_key: `dispatch` wraps `Cmd::Commit`, `Cmd::New`, and `Cmd::Push` with `render::quarantine_status` to exit 3 when secret-quarantined files were left out of the snapshot, but leaves `Cmd::Land` returning `hub_cmd::land` directly so `vl land` exits 0 despite unrecorded quarantined files.

head: c2fe202469f7a7c06825c43c0e37d8167e4c081f
answer_key: `confine::base_args` mounts allow-listed home directories (`~/.cargo`, `~/.claude`, `~/.claude.json`) with `--ro-bind` and no writable overlay layer, causing confined agent runs (`cargo`, Claude Code) that write into their caches or config to fail with read-only filesystem errors.

head: 33c18c8d1517c3dd575120babebddaad9569d92c
answer_key: The workspace socket (`ws_socket`) allows `vl commit -m`, `vl describe -m`, and `vl new -m` inside `--with-isolated` sandboxes without scanning the message arguments against `InjectedSecrets`, letting a confined command exfiltrate injected secret values into plain-text change descriptions.

head: 5b673ffba1b52eb2d57b853707fd4dac83166b30
answer_key: `ws_socket::check_revisions` wraps `ctx.rev(spec)` in `store.without_fetching` to keep sandbox commands offline, but `ctx.rev` still queries `client.tested(branch)` over HTTP for `<branch>@tested` specs, allowing a `--no-network` sandbox to make network requests to the server.

head: 72a8f35c83b898dbe030e9a66dae64f645bd4eba
answer_key: `sealed_files_in_tree` guards `EntryKind::Conflict` with `if !e.visibility.is_public()`, which is always false because conflict tree entries carry `Visibility::Public` while their terms hold the sealed visibility, leaving conflicted sealed secret files unguarded against exfiltration in sandboxes.

head: cf9739455eee861eb86057c3b5b2a5ffe585c99d
answer_key: `exec_ephemeral` waits to move secret-quarantined files via `keep_left_out` until after post-recording `--only` stray and policy checks that can return `Err`, so an error after `commit_fs_as_child_with` drops the throwaway sandbox and permanently loses the unrecorded files.

head: 7127500c5a7e12ac54e9de9468770f375e9fe574
answer_key: Persistent sandbox writable allow-list overlays are stored under `.veil/local/sandboxes/<name>/layers` keyed only by workspace name rather than workspace id, so recreating a workspace of the same name after `vl undo` reuses the undone workspace's overlay files.

head: 5b2b3c5d8e5fbe8eac8af7d1c36b56cdca21287d
answer_key: `secrets::url_syntax` requires the byte immediately before `://` to be `[A-Za-z0-9+.-]`, causing the secret scanner's `url-password` rule to miss real credentials in URLs with templated schemes such as `${DB_SCHEME}://user:pass@host` or `{{ .Values.scheme }}://user:pass@host`.

head: 8802a0a1c577fdba62b517e9656ded37e4aaab49
answer_key: The web file viewer (`file_route`) checks `used_bytes + line_len > WEB_FILE_BYTES_PER_PAGE` only when `end > start`, so a single-line file (such as minified JSON or JS) bypasses the page byte cap and is HTML-escaped whole in memory.

head: bd6568623154a80b6b84665af282f9c83b7c4329
answer_key: `Service::prepare` and `Service::commit` call `prs::verify_landing_review` sequentially per batch entry—including inside the commit transaction holding the branch lock (~190 SQL round trips per 64-entry batch)—instead of batching the review-rule queries.

head: 9aaad9d28a516ddc9c51789e5cc05f66d4708773
answer_key: `merge::merge_onto` checks whether the tip already carries the identical entry (`te == oe`) only after `merge_entry_bytes`, so identical edits to binary files, files above `MAX_MERGE_FILE_BYTES`, `-merge` paths, or directory replacements are wrongly rejected as conflicts.

head: 0d6bf3a32ed1663b50634d58f49d82ef6a823549
answer_key: The deriver's parallel read-ahead spawns worker threads via `std::thread::scope` (`sc.spawn`) with Rust's default 2 MiB stack instead of the server's 64 MiB `THREAD_STACK`, overflowing the stack and aborting the server on deep recursive `tree_changes` walks.

head: 66dff0d5a1f01f73e307f84067f26e0e020bd556
answer_key: `pack_gc::walk_from_roots` inserts `EntryKind::File` and `EntryKind::Symlink` target ids into `reachable` without enqueuing them while push validation never checks that an entry's stored object kind matches its `EntryKind`, allowing a pushed file entry pointing at `main`'s directory `Tree` id to poison `reachable` so pack GC skips walking that tree and deletes `main`'s blobs.

ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` chunks before checking whether a conflicting parent row held a different `projected_id` and returns `Ok(None)` without deleting the already-committed child rows, leaving child memos pointing at unstored parent projections.
